frontier.hypothesis: There is a C construct that gives ONE address def TWO uses and a SECOND def ONE use for the same row, without any dead statement - i.e. the row pointer has a genuine second consumer, so it is naturally live across the c- and b-stores and then re-derived for a reason the program needs.
frontier.mechanism: H-s13-8's law: flow.c:2102 grants combine's LOG_LINK only to a def that dies at its single use in the block, so the target's asymmetry (shared base at DISP8/DISP4 plus one folded LOSUM) is exactly a 2-use def plus a 1-use def of the same address value. Every form tried so far reaches two defs only by writing the same expression twice (dead) or two different expressions (banned). What has NOT been tried is a reading of the function in which the a-column write belongs to a different logical operation than the b/c writes - e.g. 'clear the flag word' as a step distinct from 'clear the payload' - so that the second def has a program reason to exist.
frontier.next_probe: Extend sweep13n.py with candidate readings in which the a-column has a distinct role (a separate clear step, a value that is not literally the constant 0 in source, a write ordered against a different condition), and for any shape that shifts the arrangement read the .combine dump via `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80062020` to confirm the LOG_LINK on the second def rather than inferring it from the asm.
